The angle $\alpha$ between the two direction vectors is given by the formula:
\[ \cos \alpha = \frac{\mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2}{\|\mathbf{v}_1\| \|\mathbf{v}_2\|} \]

First, calculate the dot product $\mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2$:
\[ \mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2 = (-3)(1) + (-2)(2) + (-6)(2) = -3 - 4 - 12 = -19 \]

\[ \|\mathbf{v}_1\| = \sqrt{(-3)^2 + (-2)^2 + (-6)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 4 + 36} = \sqrt{49} = 7 \]

\[ \cos \alpha = \frac{-19}{7 \times 3} = -\frac{19}{21} \]

The angle $\theta$ formed by the two lines is the acute angle, so we take the absolute value of the cosine:
\[ \cos \theta = |\cos \alpha| = \left| -\frac{19}{21} \right| = \frac{19}{21} \]
